# `Q-23-2` — Citation Key Not Found

> No reference has this citation key, so the citation renders as the
> key followed by `?`, in bold.

## What this means

A citation such as `[@smith2020]` names the key `smith2020`, but none
of the files listed in `bibliography` (and no entry under `references`)
defines a reference with that key.

Quarto doesn't stop the render. As in Pandoc, it reports this warning
at the key in your source and prints the citation as **smith2020?**, so
the gap is easy to find in the output. The other references in the same
citation render normally. A missing key gets no number in numeric
styles, so it doesn't shift the numbers of the references after it.

This applies to Typst output too. When Typst handles the bibliography
itself (the default for `format: typst`), Quarto checks each key before
Typst runs, because Typst would otherwise stop the whole render on an
unknown key and report the error in the generated `.typ` file.

## Why this happens

- The key has a typo, or differs in case from the key in the
  bibliography file (`Smith2020` vs `smith2020`).
- The reference is in a bibliography file the document doesn't list.
- The reference was renamed or removed from the bibliography file.

## How to fix

Check the key against your bibliography file and correct it, or add
the missing reference to a file listed in `bibliography`:

```yaml
---
bibliography: references.bib
---
```

For a Typst render, the check is skipped when Quarto can't read one of
the bibliography files (for example a Hayagriva `.yml` file); Typst
then reports unknown keys itself.
